newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Red Box (Malaysia) drops deal to sell out.
newsitem.headline: Red Box (Malaysia) drops deal to sell out.

text.p: Red Box (Malaysia) Bhd said it had terminated a deal under which it was to be taken over by a private company through an asset injection.

It said in a statement to the Kuala Lumpur Stock Exchange that the conditional sale and purchase agreement for the acquisition of the entire paid up capital of Usaha Sama Timur Sdn Bhd (USTB) for 616 million ringgit has been terminated.
"The company has terminated the agreement in view of non-compliance of conditions precedent within the time frame agreed upon," the statement said.
Red Box did not say which conditions USTB had failed to comply with.
Red Box had been planning to issue 88 million new shares at 7.0 ringgit each to USTB to satisfy the purchase.
The reverse takeover would have given USTB a 57.52 percent stake in Red Box's enlarged capital and also given it access to the stock market for further capital raising.
USTB was awarded contracts to build and operate three power plants in Kazakhstan under a 60-year concession agreement.
It was to sell the entire 670 megawatts of power generated to the Kazakhstan government at $0.065/kilowatt hour for thermal power and $0.05/kilowatt hour for hydro and wind power.
The $786 million project was to be funded by an Australian fund management company.

USTB had also told Red Box that it has been given rights to all the net profit, amounting to not less than $62.1 million a year, from the existing Kapchagay hydroelectric power station for seven years.
